title: Nursing-record features improve estimation of home-care use
summary: Random-forest analysis of 4,323 Dutch home-care clients found that recorded nursing diagnoses and symptoms added information beyond existing case-mix groups. Reported internal cross-validated R-squared for weekly care hours increased from 22.4% to 32.1% when nursing-record features were added. The result concerns observed service use at one provider, not objectively necessary care or improved payment policy. Documentation differences and underprediction of high-use clients limit generalization.

source_review.scope: Primary relevant client selection, outcome and forest/validation Methods, Results and limitations; supplementary parameter-tuning and feature-elimination details not independently reviewed. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: One randomly selected assessment per client was retained to prevent repeated-client leakage. Forest models were compared using ten-fold validation against average weekly care hours in the 28 days after assessment, with demographic/case-mix and nursing-record feature sets.
evidence.unknown: Performance at other providers, clinically appropriate care need and reimbursement-policy effects remain unestablished. The primary body describes feature elimination but its exact nesting/tuning details are in an unreviewed supplement. Care hours combine nursing and personal care, and documentation practices can vary.
evidence.ai_role: Forest ensembles learn interactions among demographic, case-mix and nursing-assessment variables to estimate recorded care-hour use; comparing feature sets measures the information added by nursing records.
